newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere mag ad chief sees 3 pct 1997 ad growth.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere mag ad chief sees 3 pct 1997 ad growth.

text.p: Bernard Bonnamour, chairman of Interdeco, the advertising placement unit of Lagardere's magazine publisher Hachette Filipacchi Presse, said his company had budgeted for growth of three percent in magazine advertising this year.
In an interview with advertising industry weekly Strategies, Bonnamour said he was "pleasantly surprised" by a forecast of 4.5 percent growth from research institute IPSOS.

"I only ask one thing, that this should be the case. I am a bit surprised -- pleasantly -- by this forecast. Our budgets do not include this perspective. We have budgeted for growth of around three percent," he said.
Bonnamour said Interdeco had seen a rise of five percent in turnover in 1996, to 1.4 billion francs of billings, of which 131 million was made abroad.
The biggest contributors were television weekly Tele Sept Jours with 480 million francs, women's weekly Elle with 417 million francs and weekly news magazine Paris Match with 254 million francs.
Bonnamour said advertisers' initial response to Top Famille, a family magazine launched last October, was positive.

"This new concept has been welcomed by the market. For advertising, the spectrum is wide -- household equipment, tourism, services, beauty... the advertising results from the first few issues are rather encouraging," he said.
